name_note: The GTDB genus matches the literature genus Lawsonella, in which Lawsonella clevelandensis is the only validly named species.

sentences.text: Lawsonella is a genus of strictly anaerobic, partially acid-fast bacteria; Lawsonella clevelandensis, formally described in 2016, is its only currently recognised species.
It is a skin-associated organism: species-level reanalysis of Human Microbiome Project data found it common in adult nostrils, and a skin survey found sebaceous scalp sites rich in it.
The organism is fastidious and missing from routine diagnostic databases, so 16S rRNA gene amplification and metagenomic sequencing are used to identify it.

A narrative review describes it as increasingly recognised as a cause of deep-seated abscesses, with a potential association with diabetes, immunosuppression and prior surgery, and a predilection for fat-rich tissues.
